title: Click a pending job to see its details
summary: On the Job Schedule, the cards under Pending Jobs are now clickable. Click one (anywhere on the card) to open a quick, read-only look at the job: customer and address, proposal number and revenue, the system with its color, total square footage and estimated hours, the scope or notes, plus the sales team, status, and any reschedule owed. It is view-only, so nothing can be changed by accident. The + Schedule button on the card opens the scheduler as before, and the small x still removes the job from the list.
howto: On the Job Schedule, click a card under Pending Jobs to open its details.
Read the job over; nothing here changes the job.
Use + Schedule from the card (or inside the details) when you are ready to schedule it.

title: Jobs now carry their system, and the calendar colors them automatically
summary: When a customer accepts an estimate, the job now keeps the system (or systems) from that estimate, so it shows its color on the Job Schedule and can pull materials and per-system numbers right away, with no re-typing. Jobs that came straight from DripJobs never had a system, so scheduling one now asks you to pick a system before you can save. The + Add Job form asks the same way. This is the fix for the schedule system dropdown that used to open blank.
howto: Schedule a job as usual; if it has no system yet, pick one in the System type box before saving.
In + Add Job, choose a System type (it creates the job's first area for you).
Estimator jobs already carry their system, so their color shows on the calendar on their own.

title: The schedule day picker opens on this month
summary: When you open a scheduled job to change its days, the calendar now opens on the current month instead of the job's first scheduled day. For a job that spans two months (say late June into July) that means you land where you are actually working. If the job has days in another month, a line at the top of the picker names them and jumps you there in one tap, so nothing looks lost.
howto: Open a scheduled job; the day picker starts on this month.
If a line at the top says days are in another month, tap it to jump to them.
Use the arrows to move between months as before.

title: Click a week's revenue to see how it adds up
summary: The revenue shown next to each week on the Job Schedule is prorated: a job's price is split evenly across its scheduled days, so a job that runs into two weeks shows part of its price in each. Click the week revenue (or tap it on a phone) to open a breakdown that lists each job, its contract price, how many of its days fall in that week, and the slice that adds to the total. Touch-up callbacks are listed as left out, since they are no charge. It is scheduled contract revenue, not cash collected and not profit.
howto: On the Job Schedule 3-week view, click a week's revenue number.
Read each job's contract, its days this week over its total days, and the slice.
Press Escape or click away to close it.

title: New left menu: fewer items, grouped into flyouts
summary: The left menu was a long list of every screen. It is now six groups (Overview, Sales, Production, Finance, Admin, and Help). Click a group and a small submenu opens with the screens inside it. Nothing was removed, just tidied: Bonus Report and Commission now live under Finance (in a Reports section), DripJobs Sync Health lives under Admin (in a Diagnostics section), Price & Material Catalog is now called Pricing, and Next Day Schedule is now called Next Day. On a phone, tap the Menu button to open the groups. Every old bookmark and link still works.
howto: Click a group like Sales or Finance to open its submenu, then pick a screen.
Find Bonus Report and Commission under Finance; find Sync Health under Admin.
On a phone, tap Menu, then tap a group to expand it.

title: Messages now shows calls and texts together
summary: The Messages tab is one inbox that merges texts and call logs into a single conversation per phone number, newest first. Use the All, Texts, and Calls chips to filter. Every conversation is clickable, even a number that is not yet a customer: open it to see the full back-and-forth and reply right there. On an unknown number you can Attach to customer (which files all of that number's texts and calls under the customer you pick) or Create lead (which starts a new lead with the phone already filled in).
howto: Open Messages and use All, Texts, or Calls to filter the list.
Click any conversation to see its full history and send a reply.
On an unknown number, click Attach to customer or Create lead.

title: Cleaner Job Schedule toolbar
summary: The Job Schedule toolbar is reorganized so the controls sit together and read left to right: the Today and back/forward arrows with the date range on the left, the Week and 3 weeks buttons right next to them, and a single + Add button on the far right. The + Add button opens a short menu with Add Job, Add Task, Holiday, and Day Off, so the four buttons that used to be spread across the bar are now in one place.
howto: Use the arrows or Today to move the date range, then Week or 3 weeks to change the span.
Click + Add on the right for Add Job, Add Task, Holiday, or Day Off.
Click away or press Escape to close the Add menu.

title: Next Day and Job Schedule now fit your phone
summary: On a phone, the Next Day Schedule and the Job Schedule no longer make you scroll sideways. Next Day stacks each crew with a heading that sticks as you scroll, shows full-width job cards, and floats any not-yet-scheduled work to the top so it is the first thing you see. The Job Schedule turns the seven-column calendar into a simple top-to-bottom list of days, with Pending Jobs in a section you can tap to open or collapse. On a computer both screens look exactly as before.
howto: Open Next Day Schedule or Job Schedule on your phone; no more sideways scrolling.
On Next Day, jobs with no slot yet sit at the top of the list.
On the Job Schedule, tap the Pending Jobs header to open or collapse it.

title: Archive an estimate (and restore it)
summary: An estimate you no longer want can be archived from its page: it leaves the list and its customer link stops working. Archiving is a soft delete, so nothing is really gone. Open the Archived filter on the Estimates list to see archived ones and restore any of them. Archiving an accepted estimate does NOT touch the job it created; the job stays on the Jobs page and the schedule.
howto: Open an estimate and click Archive. Confirm the prompt (it warns if a job already exists).
To bring one back, open Estimates, click Archived, and hit Restore on the row.
A restored estimate comes back whole, with its areas, line items, and scope.

title: Moisture vapor barrier is now per area
summary: The moisture vapor barrier used to be one switch for the whole estimate, which was wrong when only one area needs it. Now each area has its own MVB checkbox, defaulted off. Check it on the garage and leave it off the patio, and only the garage carries the barrier's cost and gets the moisture-barrier scope language. An MVB-only job is just an area on the new MVB Only system.
howto: In the estimator, tick Add moisture vapor barrier on each area that needs one.
The price and the scope update for just those areas.
For an MVB-only job with no coating, pick the MVB Only system on the area.

title: See how the price was reached, and adjust it
summary: The estimator now shows the work behind the number: the price per square foot up top, the full cost stack (materials, labor and hours, sundries, add-ons, commission, gross profit), and a plain-English line explaining how the price was calculated, including when charm-pricing nudged it under a round number. You can override the total sell price by typing a new number; the gross profit updates live and turns red below target. A reason is required to save a changed price, and going below the gross-profit floor asks you to confirm.
howto: Look under the price for $/sqft, the cost breakdown, and the one-line explanation.
To change the price, type a new Sell price; the gross profit updates as you type.
Enter a reason for the change (required), and confirm if it drops below the floor.

title: Estimates now include a 2% sundries and disposables cost
summary: Every estimate now bakes in a 2% sundries and disposables cost (tape, blades, plastic, mixing sticks, grinder consumables) on top of materials, labor, and commission, so the price covers the small stuff that used to be invisible. This changes every price by roughly 2% of its cost. The rate is adjustable in Price & Material Catalog. The customer still sees one total price, exactly as before.
howto: Nothing to do; new estimates include it automatically.
To change the rate, edit the sundries percent in Price & Material Catalog.
It shows as its own line in the internal cost breakdown; the customer never sees it.

title: Price per square foot on jobs
summary: Jobs now show price per square foot so an outlier is easy to spot. The Jobs list has a sortable $/sqft column, the job costing panel shows $/sqft next to revenue with the square footage and system behind it, and Metrics breaks $/sqft down by system (average and median) and over time. A job with no square footage on file shows a dash and is left out of the averages, with the count of excluded jobs shown.
howto: On the Jobs tab, click the $/sqft column header to sort by it.
Open a job's costing to see its $/sqft with the sqft and system it is based on.
In Metrics, check the by-system average and median and the monthly trend.

title: Preview an estimate before you send it
summary: The estimate page has a Preview button that shows the exact page the customer will get, including the scope, the line items, and the optional add-ons, without sending anything. It opens in a window over the dashboard, the accept and decline buttons are shown disabled, and a PREVIEW banner runs across the top so there is no confusing it with the real thing. Nothing is sent and the customer link stays private.
howto: Open an estimate and click Preview.
Look it over the way the customer will see it. Close the window when you are done.
When it looks right, use Send to customer to actually send it.

title: The estimator asks about blanks in the scope
summary: Some of the scope templates have blanks in them (for example the area a coating is going on, or the project duration). The estimator now asks you to fill those in while you are on site, in a Finish the scope section, and the answers drop straight into the customer's scope of work. If you saved quickly and skipped them, the estimate page shows the same questions so you can finish at the desk. If a blank is still there when you go to send, you get a clear warning first, because a customer should never read the word BLANK in a document they are signing.
howto: In the estimator, fill in anything under Finish the scope before you save.
On the estimate page, use the Finish the scope card to answer anything left, then the scope rewrites itself.
If you try to send with a blank still in the scope, confirm the warning only if you really mean to.

title: A heads-up before you start a second estimate on a lead
summary: If a lead already has an open estimate, Start estimate now asks before creating another one, so a lead does not quietly end up with three. It lists the open estimates with their number, status, and price; you can open one of those, or create a new one anyway if that is what you meant to do. Estimates that were declined or lost do not trigger the warning, since re-estimating after a no is normal.
howto: Click Start estimate on a lead as usual.
If it already has an open estimate, pick Open to jump to it, or Create new anyway to keep going.
The lead's Estimates section shows the count so you can see it before you click.

title: One estimate can cover a garage, a patio, and more, each its own system
summary: Every area on an estimate now picks its own system, so a flake garage plus a quartz patio is a single estimate and a single price. Each area is priced with its own recipe, and the gross profit target is the square-foot-weighted average of the systems in play, so a small high-margin area does not drag the whole number. The comps panel keys off the biggest system and tells you when the estimate spans more than one.
howto: In the estimator, each area row has its own System dropdown next to its square footage. Change it per area.
Add as many areas as the job has; the price, gross profit, and hours roll up from all of them.
When an estimate spans systems, the Comparable jobs panel says which system the comps cover.

title: Add-ons come from a catalog and carry a real cost
summary: An Add-ons section in the estimator lets you drop in stem walls, joint filling, upgrades, or drive time from a catalog, with the price and cost prefilled and still editable. Because every add-on carries a cost, gross profit stays honest even when you pile on upsells. Optional add-ons stay out of the total until the customer picks them, and you can see both the base price and the price if they take everything. A free-typed one-off line is still there for whatever the catalog does not have.
howto: In the estimator's Add-ons section, pick from the catalog or click One-off line to type your own.
Set the price and cost; tick Optional for anything the customer chooses on their end.
The price box shows the base total and, when there are optional items, the total if every one is taken.
Manage the catalog in Price & Material Catalog under the new Add-ons tab: set each one's price, cost, unit, and the scope paragraph it adds to the customer's scope of work.

title: Estimates write their own scope of work
summary: Every estimate now assembles a customer-facing scope of work from your real templates, filling in the square footage, the areas, and whether stem walls and past-the-garage are included from the estimate itself. It never rewrites your exclusions or cure-time language, only substitutes the job's details. It writes itself on save, and you can Edit the text by hand: once you do, it is never overwritten without your explicit Regenerate click, and if the estimate changes afterward it tells you the scope is out of date.
howto: Save an estimate and the Scope of work card fills in automatically (needs a connection; offline saves generate once you reconnect).
Click Edit text to adjust wording by hand. After that, the AI never replaces your words unless you click Regenerate and confirm.
If you change the estimate after editing the scope, a note tells you it is out of date so you can Regenerate when ready.

title: Estimator prices with just the system and square footage
summary: You no longer have to pick a basecoat or flake color to get a price. Every system's recipe now carries default products, and an unpicked flake is priced at the standard flake cost with the color left TBD for the customer to choose after the presentation. Flake job pricing now matches the price sheet: a 1000 sqft garage quotes about $5,345 at the new 52% gross profit target, and the target is editable per system in the catalog.
howto: Open the estimator, pick the system, type the square footage, and the price appears. Nothing else is required.
Leave the flake color unpicked if the customer has not chosen; the price already includes standard flake and the color stays editable on the estimate page.
To tune margins, open Price & Material Catalog, edit a system type, and set its Target GP %. Blank means the global default.

title: Customers can now sign an estimate online
summary: Send to customer on an estimate's page emails them a private link where they can review the scope and line items, tick optional add-ons (the total updates as they choose), and accept and sign by typing their name. They can also request changes with a message or decline with a reason. Accepting creates the job automatically on both the Jobs page and the Job Schedule, with the areas and work-order details carried over. The link stays private (it does not work at all) until you send it.
howto: Open an estimate and click Send to customer. Review the prefilled email and send it.
The customer opens their link, ticks any optional items, and signs by typing their name. You get a Slack and email notification either way.
On accept, the job appears on the Jobs page and in the Job Schedule's pending list automatically, and the lead moves to Accepted.
If they request changes, edit the estimate and click Re-send: same number, same link, new sent date.

title: Estimator opens over the dashboard and asks for way less
summary: Start estimate now opens the estimator in a window over the dashboard instead of a new tab. System, square footage, and an MVB switch are all it needs for a price; products, colors, and the work order live in a collapsed More detail section. A sell price or discount box shows the margin live, and comps from your own completed jobs plus an AI price read sit next to the number.
howto: Open a lead and click Start estimate, or use the Estimator button in the sidebar for a walk-up.
Pick the system and type the square footage. The price, comps, and AI read appear on the right.
Type a sell price or a discount percent to see the gross profit move; it turns red below the system's target.
Save. The window closes and the estimate's own page opens.

title: Estimates are now real numbered records with their own pages
summary: Every saved estimate gets a sequential number (EST-102026 and up) and its own page: customer info, price and margin, line items with optional add-ons the customer can take, flake color you can fill in after the presentation, and the comps and AI read that priced it. A new Estimates section in the sidebar lists them all with search.
howto: Click Estimates in the sidebar to see the list, newest first. Search by number, customer, phone, or address.
Click any row to open the estimate's page. Edit reopens the estimator with everything filled in.
Use + Add optional item for upsells like stem walls or an extra bay; they stay out of the total until ticked.
Mark accepted or Mark lost records the outcome. Sending it to the customer arrives in the next update.

title: Start estimate now carries the lead with it
summary: Hitting Start estimate on a lead opens the estimator already tied to that lead, so the estimate shows up on the lead's page and counts in the lead's value instead of floating loose.
howto: Open a lead from the Leads board and click Start estimate.
Look for the Lead chip next to the PEC Estimator title, it names the lead the estimate will attach to.
Build and save as usual. An estimate saved offline still attaches once the phone gets signal.

title: Click a lead for its full story plus an AI game plan
summary: Clicking a card on the Leads board opens the lead's page: contact info, notes, and the full activity timeline on the left; an AI read on the right with a score, the single best next step, call talking points, and ready-to-copy text and email drafts. Nothing sends itself; you copy, you send.
howto: Click any card on the Leads board. Back returns to the board.
The AI panel leads with the next action; Copy buttons grab the text or email draft (the text copy stays locked unless the lead agreed to texts).
Change the stage right from the page, edit notes, or hit Refresh analysis after a call.
Start estimate opens the estimator with the lead attached. Once OpenPhone is connected, calls and transcripts appear in the timeline on their own.

title: Metrics: new Sales section shows which ad money works
summary: The Metrics tab has a new Sales section: price per square foot by month with a per-system breakdown, speed to lead (how fast new leads get a first contact), conversion by source and campaign, and the open lead pipeline with an AI-written weekly read.
howto: Open Metrics and scroll to the Sales section; the window picker at the top applies to it too.
Conversion by source and campaign shows leads, accepted count, rate, and sold value per ad source.
Speed to lead is the median time from a lead arriving to first contact; keep it under an hour.
Click Refresh on the AI weekly read for a fresh 3-4 sentence take on the funnel.

title: $/sqft on jobs, with a Sqft field you can backfill
summary: Jobs now show their price per square foot on the job page header and on Jobs pipeline cards. A new Sqft field on the job page lets you fill in square footage for older jobs; a value you type there always wins over the estimate areas.
howto: Open a job; the header shows a $/sqft chip when the square footage is known.
To backfill an older job, type the square footage into the new Sqft field next to Price and save.
Jobs pipeline cards show $/sqft under the price when it is known.

title: New Leads board: work every lead from first click to sold
summary: A new Leads tab (next to Messages) shows every lead as a card in six columns, from New to Accepted or Lost. Drag cards between columns as you work them. New leads show how long they have been waiting, turning red after an hour, so nobody sits unclaimed.
howto: Open the Leads tab. Each column shows its count and total estimate value; the top shows open leads and open pipeline value.
Drag a card to the next column as you work the lead. Dropping on Lost asks for a quick reason.
Use the filters for source, campaign, owner, dates, or search by name, phone, or email.
Walk-ins and phone leads: click + New Lead and type them in.

title: New leads flow straight into HQ (no more DripJobs for new leads)
summary: Facebook and Google leads now land in HQ automatically the moment someone submits a form, each with an instant AI read: a summary, a 1-100 score, and a suggested next step. Duplicate submissions fold into the existing lead instead of cluttering the list.
howto: Nothing to do day to day; leads arrive on their own once the Zaps are connected.
A second inquiry from the same person attaches to their existing lead as a note instead of creating a copy.
The Leads board to work them lands next; the data is already collecting.

title: Archived jobs no longer sit in Invoicing
summary: Archiving a job now removes it from every Invoicing section and the AR totals, the same way voiding does. Cancelled jobs stop inflating pending deposits, and their public pay links go dead so nobody can pay a cancelled job.
howto: Archive a cancelled job from its job page like before; it disappears from Invoicing on its own.
The Total AR number and the section totals no longer count archived jobs.
The job itself is untouched; it is just out of the money views.

title: Day numbers now always follow the calendar
summary: Day 1 is always the earliest scheduled day. Before, the schedule window numbered days in the order you clicked them, so adding an earlier day could leave the numbers out of order. Existing jobs were renumbered too.
howto: Open a job's schedule and add a day before the current start; the new day becomes Day 1 automatically.
The little corner numbers in the day picker and the Day column on the job page both follow date order now.
Nothing to do for old jobs; they were renumbered in the same update.

title: Short notes on the schedule, like "flake portion"
summary: Each stretch of scheduled days can now carry a short note that shows right on the calendar bar, on the week run sheet, and in the bar's hover text. Perfect for splitting one job into its flake days and patio days at a glance.
howto: Open a job from the calendar. Below the day picker you'll see one note box per stretch of back-to-back days, labeled with its dates.
Type a short label (up to 60 characters), like flake portion, and Save.
The note shows on the calendar bar in both views and in the job's schedule table. Hover the bar to read it in full.

title: Pull install days off the calendar for rescheduling
summary: When a job (or just part of one) gets bumped, open it from the Job Schedule and click Reschedule. The pulled days come off the calendar and the job shows in the Pending column with an amber Reschedule badge until you rebook it. Crew, hours, and price stay on the job.
howto: Click the job's bar on the calendar to open the schedule window.
Deselect the day or days getting pulled (deselect all of them to pull the whole job), then click Reschedule.
The job shows in Pending on the left with an amber badge like Reschedule, 2 days, plus the date it was pulled from.
When you rebook it, click + Schedule on the card, pick the new days, and Save. The badge clears on its own.

title: The job page got a clean new layout
summary: The estimate is now a Line Items table with the totals at a glance, each change order sits in its own orange box with its status, and the whole page is tidier: notes and job card fields side by side, and a Save bar that follows you as you scroll.
howto: Open any job. The estimate shows as a Line Items table; click a line name to open and edit that line, then click Done.
Each change order has its own box with a Pending signature or Signed pill and its send buttons.
The Totals section at the bottom of the estimate shows Subtotal, Change orders, and the grand Total in the dark bar.
Save job now rides in a bar at the bottom of the screen, so you never scroll to find it.

title: Estimate total, Add change order, and Download PDF moved to the top of the job
summary: The estimate total now shows in the button row at the top of every job, next to Add change order and Download PDF. No more scrolling to the Estimate section to see the price or grab the estimate PDF.
howto: Open any job. The top row now ends with the estimate total, Add change order, and Download PDF.
The total updates live as you type line prices, same as before.
Add change order and Download PDF work exactly like they did in the Estimate section.

title: Job page buttons are bolder and grouped on the left
summary: The action buttons at the top of a job (Back to jobs, View Invoice, Copy portal link, View customer portal, Messages & Calls) now sit together on the left and stand out more, so they are easier to spot at a glance.
howto: Open any job. All five action buttons now sit together at the top left.
Messages & Calls is the last button in that row and still turns orange while you are on the conversation view.
Every button does exactly what it did before; only the look and placement changed.

title: The customer invoice page got a professional new look
summary: The invoice customers open from their pay link now looks like a premium brand: a bold dark header with the amount due front and center, clean line items, and clearer payment buttons. Same links, same payment options.
howto: Nothing to do. Every existing /pay invoice link wears the new design automatically.
Email or text an invoice as usual; the customer's link opens the new page.
All payment behavior is unchanged: card, bank transfer, deposit, check, cash, and Zelle work exactly as before.

title: Messages & Calls got a phone-app look and moved into the job's top toolbar
summary: The job's Messages & Calls feed now looks like a real texting app: chat bubbles with names and avatars, call summaries in a card, and a cleaner compose box. The button to open it now sits in the toolbar at the top of the job.
howto: Open a job and click Messages & Calls in the toolbar at the top. Click it again to go back to the job details.
Calls show their AI summary as bullet points; click View transcript on a call to read the whole conversation.
Type in the box at the bottom to text the customer. Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line.
The Texts and Calls cards on the customer profile use the same new look.

title: TopCoat now tells you what changed
summary: New features show up in this popup when you sign in, and the full history lives in Help.
howto: When something new ships, you will see this popup once at sign in. Click Got it and you will not see those items again.
To browse everything later, open the Help tab. The What's New card at the top lists every update.
You can also ask the help assistant (the ? bubble, bottom right) how any new feature works.

title: Pending bank transfers show on the customer invoice
summary: While a customer's bank transfer is clearing (3 to 5 days), their invoice shows it as PENDING, the amount due drops, and the pay buttons hide so nobody pays twice.
howto: Nothing to do. The customer's /pay page handles it automatically the moment they pay by bank.
In Invoicing, the completed list shows an ACH pending chip under the balance so you know not to chase that customer.
If you try to email or text an invoice that has a pending transfer, TopCoat asks you to confirm first.

title: Messages and Calls tab on every job
summary: Open a job and see the customer's texts and phone calls in one feed, in time order, and text them right from the job.
howto: Jobs tab, open a job, click Messages & Calls (top right, next to View customer portal).
Calls show the AI summary; click Transcript to read the whole conversation.
Type in the box at the bottom to text the customer. Replies show up when you hit Refresh.

title: Customers can pay invoices by bank transfer (ACH)
summary: The Pay online button on invoices now offers bank transfer as well as card. Bank transfers cost us about $5 instead of about 3 percent.
howto: Nothing changes when you send an invoice; the customer picks card or bank on the Stripe payment page.
Bank transfers take 3 to 5 business days to land. The payment records itself automatically when it clears.
If a transfer bounces, the job gets a red ACH failed chip in Invoicing and Dylan gets an alert.

title: Itemized subcontractor expenses on Job Costing
summary: Record who was paid what on subbed-out jobs, and flag a whole job as subcontracted so the crew bonus math skips it.
howto: Job Costing, open the job, find the Subcontractors card. Add a line with the sub's name and the dollar amount.
The total flows into the job's costs and profit automatically.
If the whole job was subbed out, tick This job is subcontracted; hours expectations and crew bonus then skip it.

title: Change orders that carry real scope
summary: Add a change order from the job page with a system and square footage; pricing suggests itself, materials flow to costing, and the customer can sign it online.
howto: Jobs tab, open the job, click Add change order in the Estimate section (also on the Invoicing detail).
Pick the system and square feet and the price pre-fills like the estimator; or use Simple mode for a title and amount.
In the Change orders card you can email or text the customer a signing link and watch the badge flip to Signed.

title: Phone calls with AI summaries on customer profiles
summary: Every call to or from the office number now logs on the customer's profile with a summary, next steps, and the full transcript.
howto: Customers tab, open a customer, scroll to the Calls card.
Each call shows who called, how long it lasted, and what it was about.
Click Transcript to read the word-for-word conversation.

title: Last invoiced column and a Cancelled jobs section
summary: Invoicing now shows when each completed job was last sent an invoice (red if never), and cancelled jobs live in their own section with a Restore button.
howto: Invoicing tab, completed section: the Last invoiced column sits right after Age. Red means send the invoice.
Jobs tab, bottom: the Cancelled / archived jobs card lists every archived job.
Click Restore on an archived job to bring it back to Jobs and the Schedule.

title: Job costing submit-for-review flow
summary: Non-admin staff submit a finished costing for review instead of finalizing it; Dylan reviews and finalizes, which records the crew bonus.
howto: Fill in the job's costing as usual, then click Submit for review. Your numbers lock while it waits.
Dylan sees it in the Submitted for review queue on the Job Costing page and finalizes or sends it back.
Team member hours are entered per person on the job page; they drive the bonus math.

title: Text customers from TopCoat
summary: Two-way texting from customer profiles through the office number, plus a Text invoice button that sends the pay link.
howto: Customers tab, open a customer, use the Texts card to send and read messages.
On an invoice, click Text invoice to send the customer their pay link by text.
Customers who reply STOP are opted out automatically and TopCoat will refuse to text them.

title: In-house estimator (beta)
summary: A TopCoat estimator that prices jobs from square footage and system type, using the same catalog and math as Job Costing.
howto: Open it from the Estimator button in the nav (admins and estimators only while in beta).
Enter the areas and square footage; the price suggestion comes from cost plus target margin.
Talk to Dylan before using it on a live customer while it is in beta.
